question: tips how to conserve water
retrieved passages:
passage 1:1 Take shorter showers. 2  Replace you showerhead with an ultra-low-flow version. 3  Some units are available that allow you to cut off the flow without adjusting the water temperature knobs. 4  Use the minimum amount of water needed for a bath by closing the drain first and filling the tub only 1/3 full.

passage 2:Here are 20 water-saving tips to get you going…. 1. Shower Bucket. Instead of letting the water pour down the drain, stick a bucket under the faucet while you wait for your shower water to heat up. You can use the water for flushing the toilet or watering your plants. 2. Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth. Water comes out of the average faucet at 2.5 gallons per minute. Don’t let all that water go down the drain while you brush! Turn off the faucet after you wet your brush, and leave it off until it’s time to rinse. 3. Turn off the tap while washing your hands.

passage 3:Water lawns in the early morning or later evening in 20 minute intervals. Use a broom instead of your hose to remove debris from your driveway or sidewalk. Bathe your pets outdoors in areas that need water. Install a shut-off nozzle on your water hose; a garden hose left running can waste up to 20 litres per minute. Direct downspouts towards shrubs and trees in your garden.
answer:
Here are some tips on how to conserve water: 

1. Take shorter showers and consider replacing your showerhead with an ultra-low-flow version. 
2. Use the minimum amount of water needed for a bath by filling the tub only 1/3 full. 
3. Use a bucket to collect the water that runs while waiting for your shower to heat up, this water can then be used for flushing the toilet or watering plants. 
4. Turn off the faucet while brushing your teeth or washing your hands. 
5. Water your lawns in the early morning or later evening in 20-minute intervals. 
6. Use a broom instead of your hose to remove debris from your driveway or sidewalk. 
7. Bathe your pets outdoors in areas that need water. 
8. Install a shut-off nozzle on your water hose to prevent wastage. 
9. Direct downspouts towards shrubs and trees in your garden.

answer:
Linear Bus topology is a type of network where all nodes are connected to a single transmission medium with two endpoints. Distributed Bus topology is similar to Linear Bus topology, but in this case, the transmission medium has more than two endpoints created by branching the main section of the transmitting medium.

answer: Quartiles are three points in a data set that divide it into four equal groups, each representing a quarter of the data. The first quartile, also known as the 25th percentile or Q1, splits the lower 25% of data, and is the middle value of the lower half. The second quartile, also known as the 50th percentile or Q2, is the median and it splits the entire data set in half. The third quartile, also known as the 75th percentile or Q3, splits the lowest 75% or the highest 25% of data. The difference between the first and third quartile is the Interquartile range. Data should be arranged in ascending order for this analysis.

11. Pour the mixture into an ovenproof baking dish and bake at 400°F (200°C) for about 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese has melted and is golden brown.
12. Serve hot and enjoy!

answer: To slow and tenderly cook a chuck roast in the oven, start by preheating the oven to 350º. Heat 2 tbsp. of olive oil in a large Dutch oven pot on the stove over medium-high heat. Sprinkle the chuck roast with salt and pepper and place it in the pot. Brown all sides of the meat in the pot, about five minutes on each side. Once browned, remove the roast from the pot and add chopped onions, sautéing them for 8 minutes or until tender. Return the browned roast to the pot and add 1/2 cup red wine, thyme sprigs, chopped garlic, beef broth, and a bay leaf. Bring the ingredients to a simmer, then cover the pot and place it in the preheated oven. Allow the meat to cook for 1 1/2 hours or until almost tender. Add carrots and potatoes to the pot, then continue to cook the roast, basting it with the pot's liquid every half-hour or so for 3 1/2 to 4 hours.

To steam a live lobster, fill a pot so the water comes up about two inches on the sides. Add 2 tablespoons of salt per quart of water, sea salt if available. Bring the water to a rolling boil, add seaweed (or use a steam rack) to keep the lobsters out of the water, and add the lobsters one at a time. To boil a lobster, first consider the size of your pot. An 8-quart pot can hold one lobster, a 16-quart pot can hold 2 or 3 lobsters. If you're cooking a lot of lobsters, you may need to cook them in stages or have more than one pot of boiling water. Adjust the heat if froth starts to bubble over.

answer: Signs and symptoms of alcoholic hepatitis can vary depending on the severity of the disease. In mild cases, there may be no noticeable symptoms. answer: To check a temperature gauge, you can use the ignition of the vehicle with the engine not running. Disconnect the gauge wire from the sending unit in the coolant outlet on the cylinder head. If the gauge is unplugged from the sender and it registers temperature in the 110 to 140 degrees F range, and the resistance measured matches the gauge reading, the problem could either be the sender, or that the engine is actually running the temperature that your gauge is displaying. To roast individual garlic cloves, follow these steps:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (205°C).
2. Peel and discard the papery outer layers of the whole garlic bulb, leaving intact the skins of the individual cloves of garlic.
3. Using a sharp knife, cut 1/4 to a 1/2 inch from the top of cloves, exposing the individual cloves of garlic.
4. Place the garlic heads in a baking pan, cut side up. (A muffin pan works great for this, as it keeps the garlic bulbs from rolling around.)
5. Drizzle a couple teaspoons of olive oil over each exposed head, using your fingers to rub the olive oil over all the cut, exposed garlic cloves.
6. Roast in the preheated oven for 45 minutes to an hour, or until the cloves are softened.
7. Store roasted garlic cloves in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 10 days.

You can also season the garlic cloves to taste with herbs and spices before roasting.

answer: Based on the Income Tax Act, when an asset is discarded but not sold, the scrap value of the asset can be reduced from the block in the previous year in which the asset is discarded as per section 43(6). This is done under the block concept, where all assets of the same class and subject to the same rate of depreciation are considered as a single asset. Any changes to the block's value must abide by the provisions of Chapter IV D of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Additionally, the assessee can claim depreciation on the residual value of such discarded asset, even if it's not used for the purposes of business or profession in that year and subsequent years.

question: the difference between index and etf

passage 1:If they are looking at an investment for a taxable account, will the ETF always be a better choice? Most ETFs are index-based portfolios. Traditional index funds historically have also been very tax-efficient in terms of providing low capital gains realizations relative to actively managed funds and so forth. So, a lot of the difference, if you will, between ETFs and index funds really isn't a difference. It's that they are both indexed portfolios and will tend to be fairly tax-efficient, all else equal, relative to more actively managed strategies.

passage 2:When it comes to the tax efficiency of ETFs versus index funds, ETFs are king. Unlike index funds, ETFs rarely buy or sell stock for cash. passage 3:The difference between an ETF an index fund is not as insignificant as it might seem. It isn't just about performance, or which type of fund has the best returns. answer: An index is a portfolio of stocks that represents a particular market or market sector. Most ETFs are index-based portfolios, much like traditional index funds, and both tend to be fairly tax-efficient. The key difference between ETFs and index funds lies in their tax efficiency and how investors redeem their investments. ETFs are considered more tax-efficient because they rarely buy or sell stock for cash. When investors want to redeem their investment in an ETF, they simply sell their shares on the stock market. On the other hand, if an index fund investor wants to redeem their investment, the index fund has to sell stocks for cash to pay the investor for the shares. This difference could potentially lead to extra fees and commissions for index fund investors.

Pulmonary rehabilitation is a comprehensive program that includes exercise, education, and support to help people with COPD manage their symptoms and improve their quality of life.

Based on the given passages, here's a brief answer to the question:

To change guitar chords into piano chords, you need to find the bass note of the chord, which is the lowest note in the chord. For example, a G major chord on guitar consists of the notes G, B, and D, so the bass note is G. On piano, you can play the same chord using the notes G, B, D, and F (the fifth of the G major chord).

If you're using sheet music with chords written on it, there's no need to change anything. However, if you're using guitar tablature (TAB), you'll need to translate the guitar chords into piano chords. To do this, look at the guitar tablature and find the lowest note (the bass note) of the chord. Then, count up the appropriate number of half steps to find the corresponding note on the piano. For example, if the bass note is on the D string (third line from the bottom) and the fret number is 7, you would count up 7 half steps from the open D string to find the note F (the fifth of the G major chord).

Keep in mind that sometimes notes may need to be subtracted from chords on guitar due to string organization, but this is not an issue on the piano. Additionally, piano chords may have a different voicing or inversion than guitar chords, so it's important to listen to the recording or consult a chord chart to ensure you're playing the correct chord voicing.

The recipe for spicy rice pilaf is as follows: 

Preheat your oven to 300 degrees. In a medium-size nonstick saucepan, heat 2 tsp. of olive oil. Add 1 c. of long-grain rice (white or brown) and cook until lightly brown. Stir in 2 c. of chicken or vegetable stock, 1 tsp. of crushed fennel seeds, a bay leaf, 3/4 tsp. each of ground cardamon and cinnamon. Bring the mixture to a boil, then lower heat and cover. Let it simmer until rice is tender and the liquid is gone - this will take about 15 to 20 minutes for white rice and 35 to 40 for brown rice. This recipe serves 4.

answer:
Spicy Rice Pilaf Recipe

Ingredients:
- 2 cups chicken stock or vegetable stock
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1 cup long-grain white or brown rice
- 1 teaspoon fennel seeds, crushed
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamon
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1/4 cup slivered almonds
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 300°F.
2. In a medium-size nonstick saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add rice and cook until lightly browned, stirring occasionally.
3. Stir in the chicken stock or vegetable stock, fennel seed, ground cardamom, and ground cinnamon. Bring to a boil.
4. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone, about 15-20 minutes for white rice and 35-40 minutes for brown rice.
5. Meanwhile, spread the slivered almonds on a baking sheet and toast them in the preheated oven for 10-12 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally.
6. Once the rice is cooked, discard the bay leaf from the saucepan and stir in the black pepper and almonds.
7. Serve hot.

answer: Flat screen TVs work through technology housed between two sheets of glass. In plasma TVs, cells contain gases xenon and neon, as well as electrodes which are arranged in a grid-like pattern. Advantages of a Fluid Flywheel

Fluid flywheels have several advantages over traditional mechanical flywheels. Here are some of them:

1. No mechanical damage - By allowing prolonged slipping, fluid flywheels do not suffer any mechanical damage like an ordinary friction clutch would. This means they require less maintenance and repair.

5. Quieter operation - Fluid flywheels are quieter to operate than mechanical flywheels, which can make for a more comfortable ride.
6. More versatile - Fluid flywheels can be used with different types of engines and transmissions, making them a more versatile option than mechanical flywheels.

question: what is the effect of carbon footprint

passage 3:So what exactly is a carbon footprint? In simplest terms, carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases produced by various human activities within a given time frame. Carbon footprint is usually measured in tons of carbon dioxide (CO2) released into the atmosphere. Your home has a carbon footprint if you use oil, coal or gas to heat it. That cheeseburger at your favorite restaurant has a carbon footprint: raising the beef and wheat and operating the restaurant all involves greenhouse gases. Your car has a carbon footprint, dependent on the vehicle’s fuel consumption and driving distance.
answer: A carbon footprint measures the environmental impact of an individual's lifestyle, indicating the amount of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases that are produced as a result of daily activities. It encompasses everything from the use of oil, coal, or gas to heat a home, to the emissions from a car, to the greenhouse gases involved in producing food. The average carbon footprint per person is 6 tons per year, though in the U.S. the average is higher at 20 tons per year, with a third of that created by automobile emissions. Changes in lifestyle can reduce one's carbon footprint and hence the negative impact on the environment.

question: what is unearned revenue? provide three examples of unearned revenue.
retrieved passages:
passage 1:What is Unearned Revenue? Unearned revenue refers to funds a seller receives for goods or services not yet delivered to the buyer. Unearned revenues turn up in many familiar purchase situations. When a traveler purchases airline or railroad tickets in advance, for instance, the carrier has unearned revenues until it delivers the service.

passage 2:Unearned (Deferred) Revenue, Deferred Payment. Definition, Meaning Explained, Example Transactions. Airline tickets paid for before the flight represent unearned revenues for the airline until the flight occurs. Upon ticket purchase, airline accountants credit an unearned revenue account. They debit this account when the flight occurs.

passage 3:Unearned revenue refers to money that a company has received for products or services that it has not yet provided. The money represents a future obligation, so it goes on the company's books as a liability. Only when the company has fulfilled its obligation -- earned the money -- is the liability removed and the money booked as revenue. Unearned revenue, also called deferred revenue, is common at companies that accept advance payments.
answer: Unearned revenue refers to funds a company receives for goods or services not yet delivered. This is a liability for the company as it represents a future obligation. Once the goods or services are delivered, the obligation is fulfilled and the money is booked as revenue. Three examples of unearned revenue are: advance payments for airline or railroad tickets, payments for products not yet delivered, and other services that have been paid for in advance but not yet provided.

answer: To prepare for an ultrasound, you should consult with your healthcare provider about any specific instructions they have regarding the type of ultrasound you will be having. In general, most ultrasound exams require little to no preparation. However, if you are having a gallbladder ultrasound, you may need to fast for up to 6 hours before the exam. It's important to follow your healthcare provider's instructions carefully to ensure the accuracy and effectiveness of the ultrasound.

question: how to remove spring loaded door hinges

This type of hinge is ideal for use in a door leading to the basement, garage or any door throughout your home. Insert a 5/32-inch hex key into the opening at the top of the spring-loaded hinge if your hinge has an opening at the top of the hinge. passage 1:Depending on the type of Pap testing you're undergoing, your doctor transfers the cell sample collected from your cervix into a container holding a special liquid to preserve the sample (liquid-based Pap test) or onto a glass slide (conventional Pap smear).

passage 3:How to prepare for a Pap test. Try to avoid having a Pap test during menstruation, or when you have your period. passage 1:Depending on the type of Pap testing you're undergoing, your doctor transfers the cell sample collected from your cervix into a container holding a special liquid to preserve the sample (liquid-based Pap test) or onto a glass slide (conventional Pap smear).

passage 3:How to prepare for a Pap test. Try to avoid having a Pap test during menstruation, or when you have your period. For best results, the test should be done in the middle of your cycle, 10–20 days after the first day of your menstrual period. Talk to your doctor or nurse if your appointment falls during your period. If your period is light, it may be possible to do the Pap test. Avoid having sexual intercourse for 24 hours before the test. Do not use a vaginal douche, vaginal medicines, tampons or contraceptive (spermicidal) creams, foams or gels (except as directed by your doctor) for 48 hours before the test.
answer:

1. Schedule the test in the middle of your menstrual cycle, 10-20 days after the first day of your period.
2. Avoid having sexual intercourse for 24 hours before the test.
3. Refrain from using vaginal douches, medications, tampons, or spermicidal creams, foams, or gels for 48 hours before the test, unless directed by your doctor.

It is also recommended to discuss any concerns or questions you may have with your doctor or nurse before the test.

passage 1:The Boxer's most notable characteristic is his desire for human affection. Though his spirited bearing, square jaw, and cleanly muscled body suggest the well-conditioned middleweight athlete of dogdom, the Boxer is happiest when he is with people--especially children, watching protectively over their play.

passage 2:The Boxer is a breed of medium-sized, short-haired dogs developed in Germany. Their coat is smooth and tight-fitting; colors are fawn or brindled, with or without white markings, which may cover the entire body, and white.oxers are brachycephalic (they have broad, short skulls), have a square muzzle, mandibular prognathism (an underbite), very strong jaws, and a powerful bite ideal for hanging on to large prey. The Boxer was bred from the Old English Bulldog and the now extinct Bullenbeisser, and is part of the Molosser group.

passage 3:So are breeds with short noses, like Bulldogs or Pugs, since they can't pant as well to cool themselves off. answer: Boxers are medium-sized, short-haired dogs originally developed in Germany. They are characterized by a smooth and tight-fitting coat that comes in fawn or brindled colors, with or without white markings. They may have broad, short skulls and a square muzzle, along with an underbite, strong jaws and a powerful bite. Boxers are part of the Molosser group, and descended from the Old English Bulldog and the now extinct Bullenbeisser. They are well-conditioned like middleweight athletes, with cleanly muscled bodies. Boxers are happiest when they are with people, especially children, and they have a desire for human affection. Boxers need to be trained due to their size and strength as they may accidentally knock people over. They are happy, excitable, and a bit mischievous. They are also a heat-sensitive breed.

passage 1:For people with Type 1 diabetes, however, having measurable amounts of ketones in the urine or blood is cause for concern. Ketones in a person with Type 1 diabetes may be a sign that his diabetes is out of control, he is ill or has an infection, or he is under extreme stress.

passage 2:Iron-deficiency anemia is the most common type of anemia. It happens when you do not have enough iron in your body. Iron deficiency is usually due to blood loss but may occasionally be due to poor absorption of iron. Pregnancy and childbirth consume a great deal of iron and thus can result in pregnancy-related anemia.

passage 3:Usually, menstrual bleeding lasts about 4 to 5 days and the amount of blood lost is small (2 to 3 tablespoons). However, women who have menorrhagia usually bleed for more than 7 days and lose twice as much blood. If you have bleeding that lasts longer than 7 days per period, or is so heavy that you have to change your pad or tampon nearly every hour, you need to talk with your doctor.
answer:
Based on the provided passages, here are some situations where it is concerning to be aware of blood loss:

1. For people with Type 1 diabetes, ketones in the urine or blood may indicate uncontrolled diabetes, illness, infection, or extreme stress, which could lead to excessive blood loss. (Passage 1)
2. Iron-deficiency anemia occurs when there is not enough iron in the body, often due to blood loss. This can happen during pregnancy and childbirth, which can result in significant blood loss. (Passage 2)
3. Heavy menstrual bleeding that lasts longer than 7 days or results in excessive blood loss (twice the amount lost during a normal period) requires medical attention. (Passage 3)

Therefore, if you experience any of these symptoms, it is important to seek medical attention to address the underlying cause of blood loss.

question: difference between struts and shocks
retrieved passages:
passage 1:On Automobiles we loosely use the word 'damper' in place of 'shock'. A Strut is essentially a shock absorber and a spring fitted into one unit. On some cars, the damper (or technically the shock absorber) is seperate from the spring. If the Spring and shock are mounted together as a single unit, it is called a strut. Now to conclude, a damper is any material/device in general that can absorb vibration. A shock absorber is a type of damper known as friction damper. A Strut is a shock (damper) with a spring as one unit. Dampers and shock-absorbers are the same. Both of them perform the same function- to quickly phase out the vibrations from the spring that has absorbed the shocks on road in the form of vibrations.

passage 2:A shock absorber resists the bouncing using hydraulics. That’s all it does. Struts are more complex. They combine shock absorption with steering elements and support for the vehicle. Shocks are more common on trucks and SUVs, while you usually find struts on cars. But sometimes you find both—one in the front and the other in the back. Struts are more expensive, because they are more complex.

passage 3:So, what exactly is the difference between shocks and struts? Shocks and struts are two different suspension parts that perform similar functions on various suspension systems. In strut suspension systems, the spring is held by the strut, and the strut provides structural support for the vehicle. Struts are more common on cars than on trucks and larger vehicles. Shocks, on the other hand, provide no structural support for your vehicle. They are mounted directly to the vehicle’s frame at one end and the lower suspension on the other end. Shocks are most commonly found on trucks, SUVs and vans.
answer: Struts and shocks are both components of a vehicle's suspension system, but they have different structures and functions. A strut is essentially a shock absorber and a spring combined into one unit, and it provides structural support for the vehicle. In addition to absorbing shocks from the road, struts also have steering elements and support the vehicle's weight. Struts are more commonly found on cars. On the other hand, a shock absorber, also known as a damper, is a device that absorbs vibrations from the springs that have absorbed the shocks on the road. Shocks do not provide any structural support for the vehicle and are most commonly found on trucks, SUVs, and vans. Shocks are simpler and less expensive than struts because they only resist the bouncing of the vehicle using hydraulics.

question: when to use a comma
retrieved passages:
passage 1:Commas and periods are the most frequently used punctuation marks. Commas customarily indicate a brief pause; they're not as final as periods. Rule 1. Use commas to separate words and word groups in a simple series of three or more items. Example: My estate goes to my husband, son, daughter-in-law, and nephew. Note: When the last comma in a series comes before and or or (after daughter-in-law in the above example), it is known as the Oxford comma.

passage 2:Quick Guide to Commas. 1. Use commas to separate independent clauses when they are joined by any of these seven coordinating conjunctions: and, but, for, or, nor, so, yet. 2. Use commas after introductory a) clauses, b) phrases, or c) words that come before the main clause.

passage 3:Rule 2. Use a comma to separate two adjectives when the order of the adjectives is interchangeable. Example: He is a strong, healthy man. We could also say healthy, strong man. Example: We stayed at an expensive summer resort. We would not say summer expensive resort, so no comma.
answer: Commas should be used to separate words and word groups in a series of three or more items, known as the Oxford comma when used before 'and' or 'or' in the last item of the list. They should also be used to separate independent clauses when joined by any of the seven coordinating conjunctions: and, but, for, or, nor, so, yet. Commas should be used after introductory clauses, phrases, or words that come before the main clause. Additionally, they should be used to separate two adjectives when the order of the adjectives is interchangeable.

passage 2:The BMI was first introduced by Quetlet in order to eliminate the confounding effects of height on weight. In normal adults, the ratio of the weight to the square of height is roughly constant, and a person with a low BMI is underweight for their height 16.

answer:
Based on the given passages, potential sources of error for BMI and waist-to-height ratio could include the following:

1. Accuracy of measurements: Errors in measuring height and weight can lead to inaccurate BMI calculations. Inconsistent measurement techniques or equipment could introduce variability.

2. Self-reporting bias: If individuals self-report their height and weight, there may be inaccuracies due to memory recall or intentional misreporting.

3. Age and developmental stage: BMI and waist-to-height ratio may not accurately represent body composition in children and adolescents who are still growing and developing.

4. Ethnicity and body composition: Different ethnic groups may have variations in body composition, which may affect the interpretation of BMI and waist-to-height ratio.

5. Individual variations: BMI and waist-to-height ratio may not account for individual differences in muscle mass, bone density, or distribution of fat, which can affect the accuracy of these measures.

6. Health conditions: Certain medical conditions or medications can affect body weight and composition, potentially influencing BMI and waist-to-height ratio values.

7. Sample size and representativeness: The study population or sample size in the Bogalusa Heart Study may not be fully representative of the general population, which could limit the generalizability of findings.

8. Cross-sectional nature of the study: The Bogalusa Heart Study is a cross-sectional study, which means it captures data at a single point in time. Longitudinal studies would provide more accurate assessments of the relationship between BMI, waist-to-height ratio, and cardiovascular risk factors.

9. Selection bias: The participants in the Bogalusa Heart Study may not be a random sample, potentially introducing selection bias that could impact the generalizability of the results.

10. Other unaccounted factors: There may be other factors not addressed in the given passages that could introduce errors, such as dietary habits, physical activity levels, and socioeconomic status.

answer: The difference between Tier 3 and Tier 4 engines is primarily in their emission standards and the technology used to meet these standards. To prepare baby broccoli, you can either sauté or steam it. For sautéing, add about 1 tablespoon of oil to a sauté pan and heat it over medium-high heat until it sizzles. answer: The weighted average method of inventory costing assigns an average cost to each item of inventory when it is sold. This is calculated by taking the average cost of all inventories currently available. This cost fluctuates as inventory prices change. The weighted average cost per unit is determined by dividing the cost of goods available for sale by the number of units available for sale. This cost is then assigned to both ending inventory and the cost of goods sold. This method is often used when it's impossible to assign specific costs to individual units or when the accounting system isn't sophisticated enough to track FIFO or LIFO inventory layers. The recorded amount of inventory on hand using this method represents a value between the oldest and newest units purchased into stock.

* 100g unsalted butter, softened
* 100g granulated sugar
* 4 large eggs
* 100g cocoa powder
* 1/2 tsp baking powder
* 1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda
* 1/2 tsp salt
* 150ml whole milk
* 1 tsp vanilla extract

answer:
To roast a Cornish hen, follow these steps based on the given passages:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees.
2. Rinse and dry the hens.
3. In a mini food processor, combine mustard, wine, rosemary, thyme, oil, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth.

5. Place the hens in a roasting pan.
6. Roast the hens in the oven at 400 degrees for 25 minutes with the breast side down.
7. Flip the hens and roast for another 25-35 minutes or until done.
8. Remove from the oven and let the hens rest for at least 10 minutes.

If performing CPR alone, give the dog artificial respiration after each set of 15 compressions. Seal the dog’s lips, place your hand over the dog’s muzzle to ensure the mouth is completely closed, then place your mouth over the dog’s nostrils and blow gently, watching for the chest to lift and expand. Only compress the chest to about a 1/4 to 1/3 of its width, repeating compressions at a quick rate of 15 per 10 seconds. For smaller dogs, use your thumb and fingers to squeeze the chest, aiming for 17 compressions in 10 seconds.
